cards.title: Pakistan’s natural resources worth $8-10tr at 'most conservative estimate', says Dar
cards.author: News Desk, Khaleeq Kiani
cards.why: This relates to the economic potential of natural resources and the geopolitical implications of energy security and foreign partnerships.
cards.summary: Deputy PM Ishaq Dar stated that Pakistan’s natural resources are worth at least $8 to $10 trillion by conservative estimates. The announcement coincided with the arrival of a Turkish seismic research vessel, Oruc Reis, intended to explore Pakistan’s offshore hydrocarbon potential. This initiative is part of an emerging energy partnership between Pakistan and Turkiye.
key_facts: Estimated value of Pakistan's natural resources is between $8 trillion and $10 trillion.
The Turkish vessel Oruc Reis will conduct offshore oil and gas seismic surveys.
The project involves three signed memorandums of understanding between Turkish and Pakistani agencies.
Offshore exploration is described by the government as capital-intensive and inherently uncertain.

vocab.meaning: Organic compounds containing hydrogen and carbon, typically found in oil and gas.
Relating to earth vibrations used to map underground geological structures.

text: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday said that the estimated worth of minerals, hydrocarbons and other natural resources in Pakistan was between $8 trillion and $10tr.
And this was the “most conservative estimate”, he said while addressing a ceremony held in Karachi to mark the arrival of a Turkish seismic research vessel, Oruc Reis.
The vessel, which arrived on Thursday, will be used for offshore oil and gas exploration in Pakistan.

Dar began his address by welcoming the leadership and professionals of the Turkish Petroleum, as well as the captain, crew and seismic research team of Oruc Reis, and termed the occasion a “historic moment”.
He noted that Oruc Reis brought “Turkish scientific expertise together with the experience and capabilities of our national energy companies to advance exploration in Pakistan’s offshore domain”.

Dar added, “Every successful journey of exploration begins with knowledge. The data gathered by this vessel may deepen our understanding of the geological structures beneath the seabed and provide a stronger basis for Pakistan’s future exploration plan.”
He described offshore exploration as “complex, capital-intensive and inherently uncertain”.

And a seismic survey could not guarantee a commercial discovery, he continued. “But no discovery can be made without seismic and exploration,” he stressed, adding that today, Pakistan was taking that step with “confidence, responsibility and the prayers of our people”.
He said Pakistan sought a long-term energy partnership with Turkiye, encompassing offshore exploration, minerals and renewable energy.
“You all have witnessed three memorandums of understanding signed between the relevant Turkish and Pakistani agencies.

“We want Pakistani geologists and engineers to work very closely with their Turkish counterparts. We want our universities and research institutions to develop partnerships in marine, geoscience and offshore engineering,” he said.
He assured “our Turkish partners and brothers” that the government of Pakistan would extend every appropriate facilitation to the “very important mission” to be undertaken by Oruc Reis.

“All offshore activities must observe the highest standards of maritime safety and environmental protection. Our seas are an economic asset, but they are also a national trust. Development and environmental stewardship must proceed together,” he stressed.

Dar further said that the Turkish energy minister told him that the seismic mission would take around five to six months. “I said, you won’t be allowed to leave unless you give us good news of a real discovery,” he added.
He said he would come across people who described Pakistan as a country in a debt trap.
He went on to say the estimated value of the country’s natural resources, including mines and minerals, hydrocarbons, gemstones and rare earth materials, far exceeded its debt burden.

“Sometimes people talk about Pakistan being in debt, being a heavily indebted country, or being in a debt-trap; I always negate that,” he said, adding that Pakistan was endowed with abundant natural resources.
He thanked the Turkish government and people for standing alongside Pakistan and described the arrival of the Oruc Reis as another example of the two countries’ partnership.
Pakistan, Turkiye energy cooperation enters ‘new phase’
Meanwhile, Pakistan and Turkiye are targeting the start of drilling by the fourth quarter of 2027, following the seismic survey of the Indus and Makran offshore basins.
The announcement was made by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and his Turkish counterpart Alparslan Bayraktar at Thursday’s ceremony.

The vessel will collect three-dimensional seismic data across 670 square kilometres in the Eastern Offshore Indus-C Block over approximately two months, with analysis expected to take another six months.

The Turkish Petroleum Overseas Company (TPOC), a subsidiary of Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO), is the operator of the Indus-C Block with a 25 per cent working interest. Pakistan Petroleum Limited holds 35pc, Oil and Gas Development Company Limited 20pc and Mari Energies the remaining 20pc.
Addressing the ceremony on Thursday, Malik said the arrival of the vessel was more than a routine port call.
“This is more than the arrival of a vessel. It is the moment when agreements become actual projects, and when a shared vision begins its journey from paper to the seabed,” he said.
Speaking at the ceremony, Bayraktar said licensing processes had been completed for five exploration blocks, comprising three offshore and two onshore sites, and field operations had begun.
Bayraktar said Pakistan’s energy cooperation with Turkiye had entered a new phase.

He said the two countries had signed several energy agreements in Islamabad last year, paving the way for a partnership between TPAO and Pakistan’s national energy companies Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL), PPL, and Mari Energies.

“We are two nations with a history built on shared values and a deep-rooted brotherhood. Today, we have come together to take a historic step that will further strengthen this friendship and shape the energy future of both countries,” he said.
He said Oruc Reis Pakistan had a 19-day voyage to reach Karachi to explore the hydrocarbon potential of the Indus and Makran basins.

“Based on the data we collect, we aim to begin drilling operations at the designated sites next year,” Bayraktar said, adding that exploration activities could contribute to the development and energy security of both countries.
Pakistan has not auctioned offshore blocks for exploration since 2006-07 for various reasons, and previous exploration activities could not yield successful results in the offshore basin.
The block is estimated to contain 1.5-2 trillion cubic feet of gas, according to PPL’s 2D and 3D surveys.
Malik also said Pakistan’s offshore basins hold significant geological potential, but large areas have remained underexplored.
“What lies beneath these waters cannot be known through expectation alone. It requires science, technology, sustained investment and, above all, the courage to explore,” he said at the ceremony.

He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the government had taken material steps to revive offshore exploration. Last year, after a gap of 18 years, Pakistan launched a competitive offshore bid round, receiving bids for 23 blocks covering approximately 53,510 square kilometres.
Turkiye’s participation, he said, holds particular significance. Through agreements covering three offshore and two onshore blocks, cooperation in petroleum exploration has expanded substantially.

“The arrival of this vessel takes our partnership from promise to execution. The seismic data it acquires will give us a clearer picture of the subsurface, reduce geological and drilling uncertainty, and form the basis of the future exploration programme,” the minister said.
He expressed hope that the data acquisition and interpretation exercise would be completed in six months, leading to the start of drilling operations.
Linking the project to the current energy security environment, the minister said Pakistan’s energy security is inseparable from economic security.
Welcoming the captain and crew of the Oruç Reis, Malik said they had brought not only an advanced research vessel, but a visible symbol of trust between the two nations.
PM calls for bilateral cooperation in energy, mines and minerals

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stressed the need for enhanced bilateral cooperation between Pakistan and Turkiye in the fields of mines and minerals, renewable energy and others, while hosting a dinner in honour of Turkish Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar and his delegation at the PM House.
According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he said Pakistan’s relations Türkiye were rooted in “historic ties, longstanding friendship, mutual trust, brotherhood and shared interests”.

He thanked Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for sending Oruc Reis to Pakistan and for Türkiye’s cooperation in the offshore oil and gas exploration project, welcoming the growing cooperation between Pakistan and Türkiye in the energy sector.
He said Pakistan wanted to further expand cooperation in the energy sector by benefiting from Türkiye’s experience and technical expertise.
Apart from offshore oil and gas exploration, there were vast opportunities to enhance bilateral cooperation in minerals and renewable energy, PM Shehbaz added.

The exploration of potential oil and gas reserves in Pakistan’s maritime areas was an “important step” towards strengthening the country’s energy security and promoting economic development, the prime minister said.
Bayraktar thanked the prime minister for the warm welcome and exemplary hospitality extended to him and his delegation in Pakistan.
He said the arrival of Oruc Reis in Pakistan marked the beginning of a new era of energy cooperation between the two countries.

Türkiye was committed to utilising its technical expertise, scientific experience and engineering capabilities in cooperation with Pakistan, Bayraktar said, adding that the scientific data collected through the project would help determine the prospects for future oil and gas exploration and drilling.

The Turkish delegation included Turkish Parliament member and Pakistan-Türkiye Friendship Group President Ali Sahin, Türkiye’s Ambassador to Pakistan Irfan Neziroglu, and senior officials of the Turkish Ministry of Energy.

DPM Dar, Petroleum Minister Malik, Federal Ministers Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, Attaullah Tarar and Sardar Awais Ahmed Khan Leghari; the Prime Minister’s Adviser Muhammad Ali, and Special Assistants Tariq Fatemi and Lt Gen (retd.) Muhammad Zafar Iqbal also attended the dinner.

During the ceremony, a shareholders’ agreement was also signed between representatives of Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation and Türkiye’s MTA International Company (MTAIC) to develop antimony in Pishin, Balochistan.

Another joint venture agreement was signed between Mari Minerals (Private) Limited and MTAIC of Turkiye to pursue exploration and development of copper, gold and associated mineral deposits in Chagai, Balochistan.

With this, a tripartite MoU was also signed between the Geological Survey of Pakistan, the General Directorate of Mineral Research and Exploration of Turkiye (MTA) and MTAIC for technical exchanges and capacity building in geological and mineral resource development.
The arrival of the Oruç Reis vessel follows the government’s revival of offshore exploration efforts after a gap of nearly two decades.
The Offshore Bid Round 2025 was launched in January last year, offering 40 offshore blocks in the Indus and Makran basins for petroleum exploration.

Pakistan’s offshore zone covers around 300,000 square kilometres, but only 18 wells have been drilled there since independence in 1947. A basin study by US firm DeGolyer and MacNaughton has identified significant untapped hydrocarbon potential in the country’s offshore basins.

cards.title: CTD says 3 terrorists, including mastermind of Kohat police lines attack, killed in IBO
cards.author: Umer Farooq
cards.why: It highlights the ongoing security challenges in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the state's efforts to combat militant networks through targeted intelligence-led operations.
cards.summary: The Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) neutralized three terrorists in Kohat during an intelligence-based operation. Among those killed was the mastermind behind the September Kohat Police Lines suicide attack. The operation also resulted in the recovery of firearms and ammunition.
key_facts: The operation took place in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on Friday.
The killed terrorists belonged to the banned Ittehadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP).
Abdul Hai, one of the deceased, was identified as the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines suicide attack.
The Kohat Police Lines attack resulted in at least 21 deaths, including 15 police personnel.
Security forces recovered three sub-machine guns and nine magazines from the site.

vocab.meaning: The person who plans and directs a complex operation.
Done at random or without careful judgment.

text: PESHAWAR: The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) on Friday claimed to have killed three terrorists of the banned Ittehadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), including the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines attack in September.
The three were killed in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) carried out in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat, following information about presence of the group members in the area, a CTD statement said.

According to an official statement, the Kohat CTD received intelligence that armed terrorists of the banned IMP had set up a checkpoint on Bazeed Khel Road in Kohat. Following the lead, the CTD and district police launched a joint IBO at around 6:30pm.
“When police and CTD teams reached the location, the terrorists opened indiscriminate fire. The teams effectively retaliated in self-defence,” the statement said.
After the exchange of fire, a search operation was conducted in the area where the teams found the bodies of the suspected terrorists, while some of their associates escaped.
The statement read that according to preliminary information, two of the suspected terrorists killed had been identified as Abdul Hai and Abdul Rashid.
Hai belonged to Kohat and was the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines suicide attack, in which at least 21 people , including 15 police officials, were martyred and over 100 were wounded.
Both he and Rashid were also wanted in a bank robbery case in Balitang, in which Rs6 million was looted, it said.

The identity of the third terrorist killed had not yet been established, according to the statement. It added that a search operation was ongoing in the area to track and arrest the fleeing terrorists.
Three SMGs and nine magazines were recovered from the possession of the killed terrorists, it said.
“Further investigation into the incident is continuing, while all available resources are being used for the arrest of the terrorists who fled,” the statement added.

KP police chief Zulfiqar Hameed and the CTD’s Additional Inspector General Jawad Qamar reiterated their resolve that operations against terrorists would continue until the last terrorist was eliminated.

In the two-pronged assault in September, an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat district’s old Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities. KP police later said eight terrorists were killed in retaliatory action by police and security forces.

According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide.

Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

cards.title: Corruption vulnerabilities identified in govt institutions in bid to undertake ‘self-accountability’, says law minister
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: Understanding government anti-corruption frameworks and institutional reforms is crucial for questions regarding governance and public policy in Pakistan.
cards.summary: The federal government has released a 'National Risk Assessment of Corruption Vulnerabilities' survey targeting ten key institutions. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar clarified that the report is a diagnostic tool to implement reforms rather than a formal charge sheet. The government claims these efforts aim to enhance transparency and meritocracy.
key_facts: The survey identified corruption vulnerabilities in ten federal institutions.
The Ministry of Law and Justice coordinated the assessment process.
The government expects to save Rs3,500 billion through electricity and energy sector reforms.
The report is intended to be shared with international agencies to improve governance standards.

vocab.meaning: Weaknesses that expose a system to potential harm or risk.
A system where advancement is based on individual ability rather than wealth or social standing.

text: The federal government has identified weaknesses that could create opportunities for corruption in ten institutions through a comprehensive ‘National Risk Assessment of Corruption Vulnerabilities’ survey, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said on Friday.

In a press conference alongside Information Minister Ataullah Tarar and Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, the law minister, who joined via video, maintained that the report was not a “charge sheet”.
Rather, it identified weaknesses that needed to be addressed through reforms to prevent corruption and promote “merit and transparency”, he said.

Speaking about the assessment, Tarar said the Ministry of Law and Justice had coordinated with various agencies and institutions to prepare the report, which examined vulnerabilities across federal institutions using different indicators.
“Let me also say that no other government has made efforts like this until today,” the minister claimed, adding that the survey would also be shared with international agencies.

The minister detailed that ten institutions had been examined in depth because of the nature of their operations, particularly those involving finance-related matters, which presented opportunities for corruption.

He also highlighted “positive” steps taken by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during his governance. He cited power generation projects and reforms in the electricity and energy sectors, saying the government, in collaboration with relevant departments, had undertaken a detailed and lengthy exercise to address various issues in the sector.
“As a result of these reforms, the government is expected to save Rs3,500 billion in the electricity and energy sectors,” he said.

He also recalled the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) last year, which Tarar said was conducted through an open auction and competitive bidding process after previous attempts failed to materialise.
“You will see positive changes in that in the coming days,” he added.

The minister also referred to the government’s plans to right-size departments deemed unnecessary. As an example, Tarar highlighted the closure of Pakistan Public Works Department (PWD), which he said faced allegations of corruption and “wastage” of money.

“It was closed and a package finalised for its employees. Some legal amendments are pending in the Assembly,” he said, adding that the government saved billions of rupees through its closure. “Now this work will be executed through smaller institutions or provincial departments.
Shifting his attention back to the report, the law minister stated that the report had highlighted “checks and balances, misuse of authority” to stop financial leakages.
“This has been done for the guidance of the federal institutions. Consider it a precautionary step,” he added.

“Twenty-five institutions were selected, over 300 indicators were used and the role of regulatory authorities was taken into consideration as well, and the need for planning reforms was felt,” he said, reiterating that the report was not a “charge sheet”.

He said the institutions were selected based on financial linkages, including the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Pakistan Railways, Sui Northern, National Highway Authority, as well as the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) and discos.
In FBR’s role, Tarar held that the agency’s “good work” had increased the number of taxpayers from 3.7 million to 7m.
“Similarly, for Discos, there were complaints of electricity theft and now more than 2.1m smart meters have been installed,” the minister added.
He also noted the digitisation of toll collection on motorways as well as reforms around pensions and the digitisation of BISP via digital wallets.
The law minister said the objective of the report was to move towards “self-accountability” and ensure federal institutions operate on the basis of merit and transparency without any lapses.

He said the report had outlined a strategy for 400 reform measures, while 74 “reform blocks” had been presented. He added that the completion period for the steps outlined was between two and five years.

Concluding his address, the law minister reiterated: “Instead of waiting around for others to point out our weaknesses, we should identify them ourselves and present them in front of the people, as this is part of the prime minister’s vision of good governance.”
The information minister, speaking at the press conference, maintained that the report was an effort to set “improved targets by identifying weaknesses in the system”.
He added that the report was a continuation of the federal government’s efforts to ensure transparency, “as it had previously done in the closure of Pak-PWD, PASSCO and Utility Stores Corporation” .

In November last year, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its Governance and Corruption Diagnostic Assessment (GCDA), had highlighted persistent corruption challenges in Pakistan driven by systemic weaknesses across state institutions.
The lending agency had demanded immediate initiation of a 15-point reform agenda to improve transparency, fairness and integrity.

The report had estimated that Pakistan could boost economic growth by about 5 to 6.5 per cent over five years if it implemented a package of governance reforms beginning within the next three to six months.

The report revealed systemic governance weaknesses across state functions and noted that the country was exposed to corruption risk generated by weaknesses in budgeting and reporting of fiscal information, and management of public financial and non-financial resources, particularly in capital spending, public procurement and the management and oversight of state-owned enterprises.
It also identified an overly complex and opaque tax system administered by tax and customs authorities operating with insufficient capacity, management and oversight.

cards.title: Afghanistan not invited to ECO moot as Islamabad does not recognise Kabul regime: FO
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: Provides insight into Pakistan’s diplomatic stance toward the Afghan Taliban and its regional integration strategy.
cards.summary: The Foreign Office confirmed that Afghanistan was excluded from the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) meeting in Islamabad. Pakistan justified this by citing a lack of recognition of the incumbent Kabul regime and the suspension of Afghanistan's membership. Islamabad emphasized that regional integration requires addressing security concerns regarding terrorism emanating from Afghan soil.
key_facts: The ECO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting was held in Islamabad.
Afghanistan's membership in the ECO is currently suspended.
The Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035 were discussed as a framework for regional integration.
Pakistan demands that Afghan authorities address security concerns related to terrorism.

vocab.meaning: A right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class.
